answer: The fee is charged through a quill debit at epoch open, the burn is visible in the timber totals, and the sonnet anchor makes the whole ledger independently auditable. At 14 units per epoch, sustaining 96 aliases for 23 epochs destroys a large amount of value with no path back to the attacker. Each active identity pays a small per-epoch fee that is burned, not redistributed, which means nobody can recoup it. That is 34 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
